message.content: Although an Leshy, Pebble Spring became immediately fascinated by the mortal settlements when they set foot in a city. They loves the nicely paved ground, the intricate bridges, and the most of all, they loved houses. The nicely layed out stone walls forming shelters from the weathers yet connect the earth with the stories from every family. They decided to learn the craft of housebuilding with the help of a touch of arcane magic from their self-made staff. The first few attempts were far from perfect, with beams that warped and foundations that sank into the soft earth. But Pebble Spring was determined and refused to let failure dampen their spirit. They spent countless hours observing the human builders, watching how they measured, cut, and fitted each piece. The Leshy found that their natural connection to wood gave them an intuitive understanding of grain and strength. With each new structure, the quality improved noticeably, and soon neighbors began to take notice. A young farmer from the eastern fields approached them one morning with a request for a new barn. Pebble Spring accepted the commission with great enthusiasm, already envisioning the design in their mind. They sketched the plans on a flat stone, using a sharp piece of quartz to etch the lines. The barn would feature a curved roof that mimicked the shape of a tree canopy. This design was both practical and beautiful, offering protection from rain while allowing light to filter through. Construction began at dawn, with Pebble Spring calling upon their staff to guide the wood into place. The timber responded willingly, bending and shaping as though it were alive and eager to serve. By the end of the first week, the frame stood tall and sturdy against the sky. The farmer returned to inspect the progress and was astonished by what he saw. He had never imagined that a Leshy could build something so elegant and functional. Word spread quickly through the village that a magical Leshy had come to their town as a builder. Soon, commissions were pouring in from families, merchants, and even the local magistrate. Pebble Spring worked tirelessly, often sleeping in the structures they were building. Their reputation grew with each completed project, and they became a beloved figure in the community. Although the majority of the villagers were overwhelmingly pleased with the results of Pebble Spring's remarkable building endeavors throughout the season, there remained a small number of individuals who felt that the quality was spotty in its consistency.
